assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework are the working core of modern monetary policy analysis. Staggered pricing, policy rules and the microfounded interest-rate-based framework are used daily in central banks. The effect on both theory and practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: The list is crowded: Smets, Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Gertler also have strong claims. The three-name limit forces a choice. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the unified microfounded framework) are the most identifiable originators of the core building blocks. Gali, Gertler and the Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans work are close alternatives.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and institutional adoption. The ideas date from the 1980s to the 2000s. No timing concern.
uncertainties: Who should be credited among the many eligible contributors
Whether the committee prefers to recognize the empirical medium-scale DSGE strand (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets) instead
Post-2008 and post-2021 inflation episodes may affect how the committee views the framework's validity

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the canonical account of how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It is the foundation of the macro-financial literature on credit cycles, fire sales and financial crises, and underlies much policy analysis after 2008.
assessment.attribution: The central contribution is clearly the Kiyotaki-Moore credit cycles paper. Attribution to the two authors is cleaner than for most candidates on the list. Gertler and Gilchrist's financial accelerator work is complementary, but Bernanke's 2022 prize already recognized related ideas, so I keep the proposal to two names.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of influence. Mature, with strong empirical and policy follow-up.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises may reduce the committee's appetite
Whether Gertler or Gilchrist should be added

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand labour-market adjustment, wage polarization and the distributional costs of trade. Both the framework and the empirical designs are widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson are jointly responsible for the local labour market adjustment evidence. Autor also has the task-based framework work with Levy and Murnane. Katz is a plausible addition for earlier work on skill-biased change, but the three-name limit makes the trade-shock trio the cleanest set. Acemoglu's work on tasks was recognized in part in 2024.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are from 2003 to 2016 and have had time to be scrutinized. Some replication and interpretation debates remain, which is normal.
uncertainties: Debate about the persistence and magnitude of China-shock effects
Overlap with the 2024 prize on technology and institutions
Whether the committee prefers to bundle Katz instead of Hanson or Dorn

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficient demand estimation (BLP) and dynamic oligopoly methods made empirical industrial organization quantitatively credible. They are used in merger review, antitrust, and applied work across fields. The methodological and applied impact is very high.
assessment.attribution: The BLP demand paper (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is the clearest identifiable unit. Pakes also contributed dynamic models (Ericson-Pakes) and the production-function and dynamic-estimation work. Bresnahan and Reiss have strong claims on earlier empirical IO. The seven-name list is a weakness, because the contribution is spread across many hands.
assessment.maturity: BLP dates from 1995 and is used extensively. Well confirmed.
uncertainties: Wide spread of credit among candidates
Whether the committee sees this as method versus a discovery
Choice between Bresnahan and Levinsohn, who is credited mainly for one paper

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models showed that household heterogeneity in wealth and liquidity changes monetary and fiscal transmission, through MPC distributions, hand-to-mouth households and indirect effects. This reshaped central-bank and academic modelling.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan-Moll-Violante work is the focused contribution and the three names are tightly bound. It builds on earlier heterogeneous-agent work (Aiyagari, Huggett, Krusell-Smith) that is not on the list, so the lineage needs careful handling.
assessment.maturity: The main paper is from 2018 and the field is still evolving. Less seasoned than the top candidates, though the influence is already large.
uncertainties: Relatively recent. Longer-run confirmation is still accumulating
Credit relative to earlier heterogeneous-agent macro pioneers who are not on the list
I am in the same broad field and have worked on related heterogeneous-agent models, so my judgment could be affected by familiarity

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The finding that misallocation of inputs across firms can account for large cross-country income gaps, with a tractable measurement framework, reoriented development and growth accounting toward firm-level microdata. It has a large influence on how researchers think about the sources of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the most identifiable core paper. Restuccia (with Rogerson) is credited for an independent, closely related line of work. Rogerson is not on the list, which complicates a clean attribution. I propose the two authors of the core paper.
assessment.maturity: Seventeen years of influence, with many replications and critiques about measurement. Mature.
uncertainties: Disclosure: Klenow is a long-running co-author of mine, so I may be biased in his favour and the committee may weigh this
Measurement critiques (markups, adjustment costs, measurement error) lower confidence in the quantitative magnitudes
Restuccia versus Hsieh, and the omission of Rogerson, complicate attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach to optimal taxation and the empirical estimation of taxable income elasticities connected theory to measurable behaviour. They have had a large influence on the design and evaluation of tax policy.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Slemrod are the identifiable core on taxable income and optimal tax. Chetty's contribution to the sufficient-statistics approach is substantial, but the list overlaps heavily with his work in other candidates (B021). Stantcheva's work is more recent. Feldstein, who had a major early role, is not eligible.
assessment.maturity: Good for the core, with work from the late 1990s to 2010s. Some newer parts are still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap in names with the inequality (B013) and mobility (B021) candidates
Elasticity magnitudes are debated
Strong candidates may split across related topics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion gave a tractable framework for information design and sender-receiver problems. It has applications in mechanism design, regulation, platforms and communication, and it unifies earlier strands of the literature.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the focal paper. Bergemann and Morris extended it to games and information structures (information design), which is a closely related and substantial contribution. The four-name list shows split credit, and I propose the two originators of the persuasion framework.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years old. Influence is high and growing, but empirical confirmation is less direct than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to include Bergemann and Morris
Mostly theoretical, with fewer direct tests of the framework
Recency relative to more established candidates
